property_summary: Calling NETM() by the owner preserves the caller's balance (balances[owner] remains equal to totalDistributed and specifically non-decreasing for that owner); the mutant sets balances[owner] to zero which violates this invariant for some inputs.

For any address a, after the owner calls NETM(), the owner's balance remains equal to totalDistributed (i.e. NETM does not clear balances of any address); the mutant that sets balances[owner]=0 violates this because it can reduce an address's balance to zero.

For any address k and any caller who is the owner, calling NETM() preserves the balance of every address k (i.e., balances(k) after NETM equals balances(k) before); the mutant that sets balances[owner]=0 can reduce some address's balance and thus violates this preservation property for some k.

Calling NETM() by the owner preserves the total sum of all balances (totalDistributed) — the reference keeps totalDistributed equal to the sum of balances after NETM(), while the mutant that zeroes owner balance can decrease the sum of balances and thus break this invariant for some inputs.

For any address a, after the owner calls NETM(), the balance of any non-owner address must remain unchanged (NETM only initializes owner balance rather than clearing other accounts); the mutant that sets balances[owner]=0 can inadvertently clear some other address's balance if owner==that address or due to mistaken global clear, so it will violate this for some fuzzed pair of owner and other address.

Calling NETM() by the owner does not change any account balance (balances[k]) except it initializes the owner balance to totalDistributed in the reference; the mutant erroneously increments owner's balance by 1 wei, so there exists an owner address and call where balances(owner) increases by 1 compared to before.

After calling NETM() by the contract owner, the reference contract leaves the owner's balances equal to totalDistributed while the mutant increments balances[owner] by 1, so for all inputs the reference yields balances(owner) == totalDistributed but the mutant makes balances(owner) == totalDistributed + 1 for some owner/call — the test asserts the reference's invariant that balances(owner) equals totalDistributed after NETM().
